clue.text: Sound of gong a bit intrusive

indicators.note: the sound of something is how it is heard, so the word for gong is taken by ear rather than spelling

blocks.note: a gong is slang for a medal, which is pronounced like a verb meaning to interfere
a bit of something is some of it

explanation.surface: A gong struck lightly makes a slightly intrusive noise.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal or decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone meddlesome keeps interfering in other people's affairs, which is the behaviour of an intrusive person.

clue.text: Spy in Marilyn Monroe feature?

blocks.note: first meaning: an agent planted inside an organisation
second meaning: the beauty spot on the star's cheek

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second definition as an example: Monroe's famous beauty mark was a mole.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a spy embedded in an organisation and also a small dark spot on the skin.

clue.text: Concentrated — failed to keep quiet

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: an engine that failed died
still means quiet and calm

explanation.surface: Someone focused hard but could not stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failed' here means stopped working, as an engine dies; the quiet word sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilling a liquid boils off and condenses it into a purer, stronger form, so distilled means concentrated.

clue.text: Mammoth damaged leg crossing a river

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged
crossing means lying across, so one piece straddles and holds the other

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A mammoth with an injured leg wades across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mammoth' looks like the prehistoric animal, but it is the adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoth used as an adjective means enormous, a strong synonym of large.

clue.text: Night owl determined to secure work

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it firmly inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: stout means resolute, as in stout resistance
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A determined insomniac trying to get some work done.
explanation.walkthrough: A stop-out is British informal for someone who stays out late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop-out habitually stays out late, just as a night owl is someone active late at night.

clue.text: Staff run out welcoming English conductor

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a staff is a pole, as is a mast
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Orchestra staff dash outside to greet an English conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests employees or a musical stave, but it is a pole; 'run out' is cricket scorecard shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro is the respectful title for a distinguished conductor of an orchestra.

clue.text: See 16
Colder in Canada in every respect for starters

indicators.note: starters are what comes first, so only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: the opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Canada is colder in every way, at least to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier is the comparative of icy, meaning more freezing, so colder.

clue.text: Wild cavalier is precise fighting men and women

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

blocks.note: the seventeen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A careless, reckless person is nonetheless exact about soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Special Air Service, the SAS, is the British Army's special forces regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The SAS is an elite military unit, a body of fighting troops, now open to both men and women.

clue.text: Eyeshadow for inspector?

blocks.note: the run-together word, which must be split in two; it gives no letters itself, and its two halves follow
the first part of the run-together word: to eye is to watch
the second part: to shadow someone is to follow or dog them

explanation.surface: Make-up chosen for a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyeshadow' must be split into two verbs. The question mark admits the definition is loose: a watchdog is a body that inspects.
explanation.definitionFit: A watchdog is a body that monitors an industry or authority, checking its conduct as an inspector does.

clue.text: Large ears reshaped in surgical beam

indicators.note: something reshaped has been given a new form, so the ears are rearranged

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Cosmetic surgery to reshape big ears, done with a modern beam.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasers are focused light beams widely used in surgery to cut or seal tissue.

clue.text: Backed musical about Post Office worker

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, so the whole string of wordplay is read from the end

blocks.note: the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Peron
re means about or concerning
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A backer funds a musical about a postal worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' looks like financial support for a show, but it reverses the whole run EVITA + RE + PO to give OPERATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker, especially a skilled one in a factory or a secret agent.

clue.text: At sea, if able to, this rescues people

definitions.text: At sea, if able to, this rescues people

indicators.note: at sea means confused or in disarray, so the following letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Out on the water, this vessel saves people whenever it can.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: 'At sea' scrambles the letters and also says where the boat works.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeboat is a vessel launched to save people in trouble on the water.

clue.text: Crumbs American soldier gives dog

blocks.note: both are British exclamations of surprise
GI is the usual term for a US soldier

explanation.surface: A US soldier feeds breadcrumbs to a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs!' and 'Cor!' are both mild British cries of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog, famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Athlete fired by club

blocks.note: a gun fired has shot
a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A sportsman sacked by his team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' and 'club' suggest dismissal from a sports club; they are a gunshot and a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-putter is a field athlete who throws a heavy metal ball as far as possible.

clue.text: Stupid clobber dresses man and wife

definitions.note: the answer is a noun for a stupid person; the clue word is an adjective

indicators.note: to dress someone is to wrap clothes around them, so one word goes round the others

blocks.note: to clobber is to strike hard
a man's name, short for Alfred
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Silly clothes worn by a married couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like British slang for clothing, matching 'dresses', but here it is the verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a foolish or dim person, so the word names someone stupid.

clue.text: When is a word misused? Singular needed for 8 20 motto

indicators.note: misused means put to wrong use, so the letters are put into a different order
needed says one more letter must be added to the rest before rearranging

blocks.note: the eleven letters as written
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A grammar query about misuse, followed by a demand for the singular, as if editing a regimental motto.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a grammar lesson; 8 20 is the cross-reference to the regiment at 8 and 20 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Who Dares Wins is the famous motto of the Special Air Service regiment.

clue.text: Rum delivery in case

blocks.note: rum is old British slang for strange
in cricket a delivery is one ball bowled

explanation.surface: A delivery of rum arrives in a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'case' is informal for an eccentric person, as in 'he's a real case'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball is an eccentric, and a case is an informal word for such a strange or amusing character.

clue.text: Restitution united people over time

blocks.note: at one means united or in agreement
men as people in general
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A united people make amends for wrongs over time.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the first pieces sit on top of the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is making amends for a wrong, which is the sense of restitution as repairing harm done.

clue.text: One entering used to ground that's flat

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece sits within the other
ground means crushed up, like coffee beans, so the letters are broken and remixed

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone moving into a well-worn apartment that has seen better days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' and 'flat' both look like places or surfaces; ground signals the rearrangement and flat means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flat in the sense of lacking interest or energy is dull, which is what tedious means.

clue.text: See 8
At least two gentlemen of Verona?

definitions.text: At least two gentlemen of Verona?

blocks.clueFragment: At least two gentlemen of Verona?
blocks.note: surface reading: a nod to Shakespeare's The Two Gentlemen of Verona
setter's reading: 'at least two' asks for a plural, and gentlemen of Verona are Italian, so the Italian plural form of their title

explanation.walkthrough: The Shakespeare title pulls toward the play; instead, two or more Italian gentlemen are addressed with the plural of signor.
explanation.definitionFit: Signori is the Italian plural of signor, the courtesy title for men in Italy, where Verona is.

clue.text: Hide treasure at last in South Island

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it
in places the selected letter inside the words that follow

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for south
the final letter
the Greek island

explanation.surface: Bury treasure on an island in the south seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treasure' tempts as part of the definition with 'Hide', but only its last letter is used; 'South Island' also looks like New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it in a hiding place, a less common sense beside discharging fluid.

clue.text: Dark region in Museum Brandhorst

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words, spanning their boundary

blocks.note: the end of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: A shadowy corner of a Munich art museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Museum Brandhorst is a modern art gallery in Munich; its name just supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The umbra is the fully shadowed central region of a shadow, as during an eclipse.

clue.text: Crooner Crosby with energy for boozy bout

blocks.note: Bing Crosby, the American singer
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Bing Crosby, full of energy, heads off for a drinking session.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a spell of excessive indulgence, most often heavy drinking.

clue.text: Glance from affluent alien entertaining company

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside your home, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: affluent means wealthy
the standard abbreviation for company
ET, the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A quick look from a wealthy space visitor hosting guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glance' looks like a brief look, but it is the verb meaning to bounce off at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet or stone that glances off a surface rebounds at an angle, which is to ricochet.

clue.text: Friend popular bringing tea round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: char or cha is British slang for tea
something popular is in

explanation.surface: A well-liked pal brings round a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: China means mate from Cockney rhyming slang, china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china plate stands for mate, so china is a pal.

clue.text: Slight noise made by drinker endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: a loud sucking sound when drinking

explanation.surface: A faint sound comes from someone drinking without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective modifying noise, but it is the noun for an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an insulting remark, and a slight is likewise a snub or disparaging slight on someone.

clue.text: Bug inside container with eastern fruit

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: a tin is a metal container
to bug someone is to annoy or anger them
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: An insect found inside a tin of oriental fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' reads as an insect but is the verb meaning to annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small loose-skinned citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin orange.

clue.text: What drug seller can say for example?

definitions.note: a cryptic definition of the two words I DEAL

blocks.note: first meaning: a dealer describing their trade
second meaning: a perfect model to follow

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as I DEAL, which a dealer might say of themselves; read whole it is a noun meaning a model.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example or standard, as in 'the ideal of a good citizen'.

clue.text: Artist embracing explosive goddess

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: A painter hugging a fiery-tempered deity.
explanation.walkthrough: A Royal Academician is a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts, so crosswords use the initials for any artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhea is the Titan goddess of Greek myth, mother of Zeus and the other Olympians.

clue.text: Supporter brings complaint about new player

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a beef is a grievance
N is the abbreviation for new
an actor plays a part

explanation.surface: A sponsor grumbles about a newly signed player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests a sports signing, but it is a stage performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor gives money or help to a person or cause, so is a supporter of it.
